audit_title: MIFlu NLinear Data-Leakage and Prediction-Curve Forensic Audit
mode: read-only (no figure/DOCX/PDF edits, no retrain, no rerun Test, no deletions)

headline_answer.why_curve_close: The displayed curve is a rolling one-week-ahead (lead-1 / step-0) seed-mean slice, NOT a fixed-origin full L-week forecast. ILI is highly autocorrelated (lag-1 corr 0.971) and NLinear anchors its output at the last observed input value (last = x[:,:,-1:]; y = Linear(s) + last). A 1-week-ahead forecast of a highly persistent series is therefore naturally close to ground truth.

1_why_close.answer: Lead-1 (1-week-ahead) rolling seed-mean + high ILI autocorrelation + NLinear last-value anchoring. corr(pred,truth)=0.977 (L24) / 0.980 (L60); corr(pred,truth[t-1])=0.994 (the anchor). This is legitimate strong short-horizon performance, not leakage.

2_rolling_lead1_vs_full_L.answer: Rolling lead-1, NOT a single fixed-origin full L24/L60 forecast. Each target week has exactly one forecast origin (origin = target - 104), aggregated only across 10 seeds.

3_step0_equals_lead1.answer: Yes. Zero-based step 0 == one-based lead_weeks 1 == 1-week-ahead. Confirmed in test_eval.py (lead_weeks = step + 1) and final_test_figures.py (lead1_curve filters lead_weeks == 1).

4_seed_mean_improvement.answer: Seed-mean reduces lead-1 ILITOTAL MSE by 11.5% (L24), 14.2% (L36), 13.1% (L48), 13.7% (L60) relative to the mean of individual-seed MSEs, via error cancellation. This is a genuine, modest smoothing, not artificial.

5_input_contains_target.answer: No. Input = [origin, origin+103]; target starts at origin+104. max(input_timestamp) < target_timestamp strictly. input_target_overlap_count = 0, future_target_leakage_count = 0.

6_scaler_train_only.answer: Yes. ScalerBundle.fit_from_train uses data[:717] only (population std ddof=0 + 1e-8, float32). Fresh fit == persisted scaler exactly; assert_consistent_with passes; _self_check asserts train_end==717.

7_checkpoint_val_only.answer: Yes. Checkpoint = best_val_mse (validation MSE), best_epoch=1, patience=7, early stopping on validation loss only. Test (819..1024) never influences checkpoint/seed/hyperparameters. test_eval.py performs inference only (no optimizer step).

8_plot_reads_truth_twice.answer: No. final_test_figures.py lead1_curve plots y_true_physical (solid) and y_pred_physical_seed_mean_lead1 (dashed) as separate columns from the figure-source CSV. The source CSV's y_pred is the seed-mean of per-seed predictions, not a copy of truth.

9_predictions_equal_or_shifted_truth.answer: No. exact_equality_rate = 0.0 (pred never equals truth). corr signature proves anchoring, not copying: corr(pred, truth[t-1]) 0.994 > corr(pred, truth) 0.977 > corr(pred, truth[t+1]) 0.920 > corr(pred, lag52) 0.49-0.82. A copy would give corr=1.0 with equality.

10_pte_pie_official_or_representative.answer: REPRESENTATIVE displayed-curve (seed-mean lead-1) metric, NOT the official season/event-level PTE/PIE. L24 PTE=1wk PIE=0.17%; L60 PTE=1wk PIE=0.97%. The report §5.4 already frames these as representative-curve ('代表曲线') values. The official season-level PTE/PIE and joint-hit rates live in final_peak_metrics.csv / final_peak_hit_rates.csv.

11_matches_fig_q1_step_sweep_step0.answer: EQUIVALENT WITH DOCUMENTED DIFFERENCE. Same semantics (rolling lead-1 / step-0 seed-mean ILITOTAL physical), different model (NLinear vs MIFlu GPT-2) and cosmetic style (colors/peak markers).

12_report_fix_needed.answer: YES, wording only (no leakage). The individual NLinear L24/L60 panel captions say only 'solid = ground truth, dashed = prediction'; they should state 'lead-1 (1-week-ahead) rolling seed-mean'. Prepared as remediation_plan_if_needed.md; NOT executed per the no-modification rule.

required_conclusions.6_checkpoint_val_only: PASS — best_val_mse early stopping on validation
required_conclusions.9_pte_pie_official_or_illustrative: PASS WITH CLARIFICATION — representative displayed-curve metric
